entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Benson County, North Dakota (1890-1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- Formed 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties. County seat: Minnewaukan.
- Population: 1890: 2,460; 1900: 8,320; 1910: 12,681; 1920: 13,095; 1930: 13,327 (FamilySearch Wiki, Benson County Genealogy page).
- Maddock (Reuben Spriggs's birthplace) is an incorporated city within the county; Esmond and Flora in the county had Norwegian-language Lutheran congregations per volume_search coverage.
- Spirit Lake (Devils Lake/Fort Totten) Indian Reservation lies mostly within Benson County.

## Boundary changes
No boundary changes affecting the 1890-1930 period; the county's boundaries were stable after 1883 organization.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- County-level birth records from late 1890s, marriage from late 1800s, death from 1895, all at the Clerk of District Court (FamilySearch Wiki, Benson County Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy).
- Statewide registration began 1907 for births/deaths (general compliance by 1924) and 1925 for marriages (FamilySearch Wiki, North Dakota Vital Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records).
- No FamilySearch birth/death collection indexed online for this county/period; the state has not supplied birth or death records to FamilySearch. Order certified copies from ND Health and Human Services, or search county office directly.
- North Dakota, County Marriages 1872-2000 (FamilySearch collection 2550852) covers the period with index & images.
- Pre-registration alternative: church baptism/burial records (see Church records below).

### Church records
- Lutheran congregations recorded in Esmond, Benson County (1830-1958, Norwegian/English, volume imageGroupNumber 100881428, 36% indexed, browse-heavy) and Flora, Benson County (1820-1997, imageGroupNumber 100881427, 34% indexed) per volume_search.
- U.S. Evangelical Lutheran Church in America Records 1875-1940 at Ancestry (index & images, $).
- Both congregation volumes are mostly browse-only images; records partly in Norwegian.

### Census records
- Federal census: 1890 did not survive nationwide; next available is 1900 (collection image group 004120517, 92% indexed). 1910, 1920, 1930 federal censuses also apply but were not directly queried here.
- State/territorial census: 1915 (FamilySearch collection 2346284, also ND image group 007637091/007637092, 51-55% indexed) and 1925 (FamilySearch collection 2351024).
- 1885 Dakota Territory census index available at NDSU Archives and FamilySearch Catalog (koha:655787, partial index to Benson County).

### Probate and court records
- Probate/court records held at county clerk's office from 1883 per the county wiki Record Dates table.
- North Dakota and South Dakota Wills and Probate Records 1878-1928 at Ancestry (index & images, $). FamilySearch Full-Text Search also covers wills/probate, dates vary.
- Determine testate/intestate status once an identified candidate father/mother is found, to target wills vs. administrations.

### Land records
- Public-domain rectangular survey land; homesteading was the primary means of acquiring county land (FamilySearch Wiki, North Dakota Land and Property).
- BLM Land Patent Search (federal patents/homesteads, some images) and Benson County BLM Land Records Index at USGenWeb Archives.
- U.S. Homestead Records 1863-1908 and U.S. General Land Office Records 1796-1907 at Ancestry ($).
- Deeds/mortgages recorded by the county Register of Deeds from 1883.

### Military records
- WWI (1917-1918): North Dakota Military Men and WWI service rosters at Ancestry ($); Benson County WWI Casualties list at Genealogy Trails.
- No Civil War-era county-specific need expected for this family's generation, but Dakota Territory Civil War Service Records (1861-1865) exist statewide if needed for an earlier generation.

### Cemetery records
- North Dakota, Cemetery Records 1877-1999 (FamilySearch collection 1451475, 594,509 persons) covers the county.
- FindAGrave, BillionGraves, Interment.net and USGenWeb Tombstone Project all list Benson County cemeteries.

### Newspaper records
- Chronicling America has North Dakota newspapers 1777-1963 (free). GenealogyBank (1865-1931) and NewspaperArchive (1873-1994) are subscription options.
- Maddock-specific items: Maddock High School Graduates 1917-1925 at Genealogy Trails; "The First Fifty Years: a history of the community of Maddock, North Dakota, 1901-1951" (FamilySearch Catalog koha:2205557, available online) may include family/biographical detail relevant to a family resident in Maddock circa 1898.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Benson County naturalization case files are extensive: Declarations of Intention 1884-1954, Final/Second Papers 1888-1955, Miscellaneous Naturalization Records 1903-1955 (FamilySearch Catalog koha:1009663, koha:998987, koha:1009683) - all full-text searchable online though 0% name-indexed (volume_search image groups 007785641-45).
- North Dakota, Manifests of Immigrant Arrivals 1910-1952 (FamilySearch collection 2443935) and US Border Crossings from Canada 1894-1954 (FamilySearch collection 2185932) apply if the family emigrated via Canada, a common route into this part of North Dakota.

### Tax records
- County tax records at the county treasurer's/auditor's/clerk's office; some moved to the North Dakota State Archives (FamilySearch Wiki, Benson County Genealogy).

### Other record types
- School records: Maddock High School Graduates 1917-1925 at Genealogy Trails (too late for Reuben's own schooling circa 1904-1912, but could help locate contemporaries/witnesses).
- Local histories: Knox area history (koha:185094); Oberon N.D. 1884-1990 (koha:1006119); Minnewaukan Illustrated (koha:2227724, online) - useful county-context biographical sources.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | County Marriages 1872-2000; Cemetery Records 1877-1999; Census 1915/1925; Naturalization Records 1868-1924; Manifests of Immigrant Arrivals 1910-1952 | No state birth/death records supplied to FamilySearch | Free |
| Ancestry | North Dakota and South Dakota Wills and Probate Records 1878-1928; ND State Death Certificates 1908-2007; Territorial and State Censuses 1885/1915/1925 | Fills probate and post-1908 death gap | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | North Dakota Marriages 1770-Onward; North Dakota Deaths 1893-Onward | Index-only alternative to Ancestry's certificates | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search returned 13 digitized volumes for Benson County 1890-1930 (census, naturalization, church, probate, court, etc.); all 13 were detailed above (totalResults equaled the page).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Benson County Courthouse, Minnewaukan, ND | Birth records from late 1890s, marriage from late 1800s, divorce/probate/court from 1895, land records at Register of Deeds | In-person / mail; 701-473-5345 |
| North Dakota State Archives, Bismarck | Microfilm of original Benson County naturalization records; some tax records | In-person / inter-library loan |
| ND Health and Human Services, Bismarck | State birth/death certificates (restricted access) | Mail request, relative-only access |

## Records NOT online
- Birth and death certificates: FamilySearch has not acquired any ND birth or death records from the state; order from ND Health and Human Services or search county office.
- Pre-1925 marriage license originals for Benson County are not confirmed among the state archive's online-indexed counties list (which names other counties); contact the county directly.

## Known record losses
- The 1890 federal census for North Dakota did not survive (FamilySearch Wiki, Benson County Genealogy, Census Records section) - a nationwide loss, not county-specific.
- No known courthouse disaster/record loss is recorded for Benson County itself (FamilySearch Wiki, Record Loss section).

## Research tips
- Finding parents: ND death records (1923 onward) recorded the deceased's birth/parent info, but accuracy depends on the informant's memory and relationship (North Dakota Research Tips and Strategies, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- Obituaries can name parents and family members - check Chronicling America and county-specific obituary indexes (same source).
- Knowing the family's church denomination narrows which congregation's baptismal/burial records to search (same source).
- Check every census year 1900-1930 for the family; relationship-to-head-of-household was recorded from 1880 onward (same source).
